emma: Quick share — ran an "early-token priority" prefetch probe on a draft llama3-13b quant build. Wanted a short sanity check on perf vs quality before we scale the run. TL;DR: ~18% median token latency reduction, throughput +12%, tiny QA regressions concentrated in long answers.

sasha: Nice. Which decoding and dataset? top-p/temp?

emma: Dataset = onboard-eval-1k (mixed QA/instructions/coding). Decoding: greedy for deterministic comparison, plus a couple of temp=0.7 runs. Speculative config = early-prefetch, window=8, model=llama3-13b-q4_0. HW = A100-80GB, per-GPU batch=8.

morgan: Raw numbers when you have them?

emma: pasted quick outputs below (summary):

```
model: llama3-13b-q4_0
baseline: standard greedy
speculative(early, w=8):
median token latency: baseline 24.5ms -> spec 20.1ms (-18%)
p50 p95 p99: baseline 24.5 46.7 132.3 -> spec 20.1 39.4 118.0
throughput (tokens/s): 115k -> 128.8k (+12%)
quality (EM exact match on openQA subset): baseline 72.3% -> spec 71.8% (-0.5pp)
BLEU avg: 34.2 -> 33.7 (-0.5)
notes: regression concentrated in long-form answers (>150 tokens); short answers stable.
fallback rate (token-level misprediction -> fallback decode): 2.2% tokens
full-sequence fallback rate: 0.6% of requests
```

liam: any safety or hallucination differences?

emma: safety flags up +0.1% FP, not stat sig with 1k sample. Hallucination counts (model inventing facts) ticked up on long generative tasks, correlates with the QA EM drop.

katie: Did you try a late-prefetch variant for comparison?

emma: yes — late-prefetch (align prefetch to last tokens) yields similar throughput (+10%) but larger QA hit (~-1.3pp). Hypothesis: early-prefetch stabilizes prefix KV cache and reduces overwrites; late-prefetch increases mismatch for long-context continuations.

sasha: How did you simulate rollout behavior (fallbacks, KV misses)?

emma: A/B replay of 100k anonymized production traces with session continuity. Toggle speculative on subset, record token fallbacks and KV hit/miss. Observed that while token-level misprediction is ~2.2%, only a small fraction cause sequence-level fallbacks because we resolve via local patching.

morgan: logs / commands you used?

emma:
```
./run_eval.sh --model llama3-13b-q4_0 --speculative early --window 8 --dataset onboard-eval-1k --out /tmp/spec-early.json
cat /tmp/spec-early.json | jq '.metrics | {p50,p95,p99,throughput,EM,BLEU,token_fallback_rate,seq_fallback_rate}'
```

emma: Next steps I propose:
- run on T4/RTX-class for cost-proj
- expand to 10k prompts incl. instruction-following + harmful-content suite
- sweep window sizes (w=4,8,12) and record per-length quality delta
- run with q5_0-ish quant (q5_0 or q5_maybe) to check quant+spec interactions
- instrument token-level KL drift and per-token confidence vs baseline for diagnosing regressions

sasha: also try mixing speculative with small-batched immediate-decoding (two-stage) to see if that reduces sequence fallbacks.

liam: :thumbsup:

eval-bot: New artifact uploaded: /artifacts/2418000000/spec-early-summary.json (metrics + raw traces, anonymized).

emma: thanks — will kick off the 10k run once we confirm quant matrix. tagging @katie for scheduling infra run. :eyes:
